exception.reason: There is no rate limiting on /api/auth/login inside the app. A network or edge rate limiter is expected to sit in front of it in production, and this reference app does not ship the deployment layer that would provide one, so the control is out of its own boundary rather than forgotten.
exception.compensatingControl: Password hashing costs per attempt (backend/app/auth.py); docs/runbook.md names the edge rate limiter as a deployment prerequisite.

requirements.statement: Mutating requests cannot be forged from another origin on the cookie-authenticated web path

exception.reason: There is no CSRF token on the web path. Mitigated by samesite lax on the session cookie and a required application/json content type on every mutating request. The native client is not exposed at all: it never sends the cookie, only a bearer token, which a cross-site request cannot forge.
exception.compensatingControl: samesite=lax on the session cookie (backend/app/auth.py), a JSON-only mutation surface, and a bearer-token path that carries no ambient credential.

requirements.statement: The session signing secret can be rotated without logging every user out

exception.reason: There is a single SESSION_SECRET and no grace-period rollover with two valid keys, so rotating it invalidates every session at once, cookie and bearer token alike. Accepted at this app's size: the operational cost is a forced re-login, which docs/runbook.md documents as the expected consequence.
exception.compensatingControl: docs/runbook.md states the blast radius of a rotation, so an operator is not surprised by it.

requirements.statement: A concurrent edit made on another device is never silently discarded
requirements.source: docs/sync-contract.md, What this contract does not promise

exception.reason: Last-write-wins by server clock can discard the content of the losing edit without telling anyone. This is the deliberate trade-off for a single-user task list, where two devices editing the same row at the same moment is rare and the cost of merge machinery is not. A multi-user product would not be allowed to accept this.
exception.compensatingControl: The rule is stated in docs/sync-contract.md rather than left implicit, and the stale-edit rejection path is tested (backend/tests/integration/test_sync.py::test_push_update_conflicts_when_client_edit_is_stale), so the loss is bounded to the content of a losing edit and never to a whole row.
